brief: A wall clock with hands that turn and tell the time.

requirements.requirement: A wall clock (a clock face mounted on a wall)
requirements.evidence: No clock part or prop exists in the catalog or props list (find_props 'clock' returned nothing). The build is still the single starting piece; nothing was placed.

requirements.requirement: Hands that turn and tell the time
requirements.evidence: The catalog has no hand, pointer, spindle or pivot part. The only rotating-looking item is the spool axle, which exists to hang a filament spool between two facing rod sockets, not to drive a clock hand, and find_sockets reports no axle offers on the current build. Nothing in the system provides a centred rotating shaft with a time-keeping gear or stop.

finish.summary: I did not build the clock. Hex Cluster is a modular bin, base, cover and notch system; it has no clock face, hand, spindle or pivot part that could rotate and show the time, so a working wall clock cannot be assembled from it, and I left the build unchanged. What the system could do is a static wall-mounted hex panel or a shelf-style display (bases with covers and trays) that you could use as a mount or dial backing for a clock movement bought separately, which is outside this system. Note also that the configurator checks fit and collisions only, not the strength or mounting of a wall fixing.
